_comment: LINEDOWN — GENUINE reference marking fixture for the SCHEDULE-REJECTED candidate (cand-04).
Included for completeness of the genuine reference set: all three tier-1 modules the desk
actually considered have a clean marking record on file. This one also makes the point that
cand-04 was rejected on LEAD TIME ALONE — there is nothing wrong with the part, its markings
are clean, and it stays on the QVL. A schedule reject is not a quality reject.
ILLUSTRATIVE: marking strings, lot codes and serial ranges are plausible and format-correct
but fabricated. Not transcribed from real SK hynix parts.
MODULE vs DIE: describes markings on a complete 288-pin RDIMM assembly. The component part
number under `dramPackageTopMarking` is recorded because it is physically printed on the
packages, NOT because anything here substitutes die.
No SVG label was authored for this fixture — it is not shown in beat 5, which compares the
suspect lot against the Micron incumbent (the part it claims to be) and the Samsung winner
(the low-similarity control). Text only is correct here.
dispositionNote: Rejected in this run on schedule only — 14-week factory lead time against an 11-day kit date. Remains qualified on the QVL.

moduleLabel.substrate: white polyimide adhesive label, heat-spreader mounted

dramPackageTopMarking.surfaceFinish: uniform moulded epoxy, no abrasion, consistent gloss
dramPackageTopMarking.note: The marked die revision M corresponds to the module build recorded in validation report MV-G4-0291. It is a descriptor of what was on the bench, NOT a substitutable attribute. The superseded A-revision build (HMCG94AGBRA109N) is a separate MPN and is withdrawn from the QVL.

plain: A third genuine example, from the supplier we turned down purely because it could not deliver in time. Its markings are perfectly clean — we said no to the schedule, not to the part.
